title: arXiv Mathematics — daily notable papers, 6 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv supplies no official trending chart. This is an inferred notable-paper ordering, not a readership ranking; attention and citation evidence for this fresh batch is limited, and the preprint claims have not all received expert review.

sections.title: Tusnády's problem and online two-sample thinning
sections.abstract: The paper establishes sharp discrepancy orders for Tusnády's problem in every fixed dimension at least two, then applies them to online two-sample thinning, obtaining sharp prefix bounds and a one-dimensional terminal order.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves the largest box discrepancy is Θ_d((log N)^(d−1/2)) for each fixed d≥2, and gives a Θ_{k,ρ}((log n)^(k+1/2)) minimax expected prefix discrepancy for fixed k≥1 and 0<ρ<2; in one dimension the terminal order is Θ_ρ((log log n)^(3/2)).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Dimensions are fixed as N or n grows; the online model uses two independent samples from a common unknown Borel distribution and an expected deletion budget ρn, with 0<ρ<2.
sections.unique_caveat: For k≥2, the paper's terminal online-thinning lower and upper bounds still differ by a factor of log n; the author identifies closing this gap as open.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across combinatorics, algorithms, and probability; matches Nikolov's upper bound with a sharp fixed-dimension order and connects that result to minimax online-thinning bounds.

sections.title: Hyperpolarity of polar foliations of codimension two
sections.abstract: For compact simply connected irreducible symmetric spaces of rank at least two, the author proves codimension-two polar foliations are hyperpolar and identifies the exceptional Cayley-plane cases.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves every codimension-two polar singular Riemannian foliation on a compact simply connected symmetric space of rank at least two is hyperpolar. For the specified irreducible spherical Coxeter quotients on the Cayley plane, every foliation is congruent to one of two known homogeneous models.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The main theorem assumes a compact, simply connected, irreducible symmetric space of rank at least two and a codimension-two polar singular Riemannian foliation.
sections.unique_caveat: This closes the codimension-two case in the stated compact symmetric-space setting; it is not a classification of polar foliations on arbitrary ambient manifolds.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The introduction identifies codimension two as the remaining open case of a named hyperpolarity problem and says the result settles it without a homogeneity assumption; it gives a rigidity classification for the Cayley-plane exception.

sections.title: Weak uniqueness for the stochastic heat equation with nondegenerate diffusion: the full Hölder regime
sections.abstract: The author proves weak well-posedness for a scalar stochastic heat equation on the one-dimensional torus with uniformly nondegenerate diffusion coefficients of every positive Hölder order, and extends the result to specified measurable drifts.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves existence and uniqueness in law for the scalar equation with uniformly nondegenerate, bounded Hölder diffusion of any positive order, and gives further uniqueness results for unbounded diffusion with bounded initial data and for measurable drifts of linear growth under the stated hypotheses.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The core theorem concerns the scalar stochastic heat equation driven by space-time white noise on the one-dimensional torus, deterministic L² initial data, and a uniformly nondegenerate bounded diffusion coefficient that is Hölder continuous with some exponent β>0.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper proves weak uniqueness, not pathwise uniqueness. Its unbounded-diffusion extension assumes bounded initial data; the author says relaxing this to L² initial data may require a finer near-time-zero argument.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The author states the result resolves the full positive-Hölder weak-uniqueness range beyond the author's previous exponent-above-two-thirds result; the arXiv comment links a Lean formalization.

sections.title: On a problem due to Erdős concerning w₁(n)
sections.abstract: For the function w defined from the prime-power factorization of n, the author answers Erdős's question about the number V(x) of distinct values w(n) for n≤x by proving its lower density is positive in the liminf sense.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves liminf_{x→∞} V(x)/x > 0, where V(x)=|{w(n):1≤n≤x}| and w(n)=Σ_{p^α∥n} n/p^α for n>1, with w(1)=0.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The setting is the specified arithmetic function on positive integers and the count of its distinct values up to x.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract establishes a positive lower density in liminf, but does not state an exact limiting density or a full asymptotic formula for V(x).
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract identifies the question as an Erdős problem left open in a 1980 source and says it also appears in Guy's unsolved-problems book; the positive-liminf bound is stronger than merely disproving V(x)=o(x).

sections.title: On do Carmo's Question: The Properly Embedded Case
sections.abstract: The author proves that every complete noncompact, two-sided, properly embedded constant-mean-curvature hypersurface of finite Morse index in Euclidean space is minimal, in every dimension and without curvature or volume-growth bounds.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves the stated hypersurface must be minimal; the abstract outlines a weighted-volume argument combined with stability outside a compact set.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The hypersurface is complete, noncompact, two-sided, properly embedded, has constant mean curvature, and has finite Morse index in Euclidean space.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is specifically for properly embedded hypersurfaces; the abstract does not claim the corresponding result for general immersed or nonproper hypersurfaces.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in geometry and analysis; resolves the properly embedded case of a named finite-index question without imposing curvature or volume-growth bounds.

sections.title: Necessary and sufficient conditions for the self-normalized central limit theorem for independent triangular arrays
sections.abstract: For rowwise independent triangular arrays, the authors derive consequences of a self-normalized normal limit and, combined with earlier work, obtain necessary and sufficient conditions for the self-normalized central limit theorem, resolving a conjecture for independent sequences.
sections.claimed_result: The authors show that S_n/V_n converging in distribution to N(0,1) forces max_i |X_{n,i}|/V_n to converge to zero in probability and V_n²/b_n² to converge to one for any median b_n² of V_n²; together with Shao (2018), this yields the stated characterization.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The array is rowwise independent, S_n is the row sum, and V_n² is the sum of squared entries; the characterization is for independent sequences, not general dependence.
sections.unique_caveat: Dependence across entries is not covered by the stated result, and the abstract's characterization relies in part on Shao's earlier theorem.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract gives an explicit necessary-and-sufficient characterization and says it resolves Shao's conjecture for independent sequences; it also states two consequences of the self-normalized normal limit.

sections.title: Classification of cohomogeneity one steady gradient Ricci solitons in dimension four and five
sections.abstract: The authors prove a uniqueness conjecture for an Appleton soliton and classify non-Ricci-flat κ-noncollapsed cohomogeneity-one steady gradient Ricci solitons in dimensions four and five, up to finite cover.
sections.claimed_result: The authors state that in dimension four the soliton must, after a finite cover, be the Bryant soliton or Appleton's noncollapsed four-dimensional steady soliton; in dimension five it must be the Bryant soliton or a soliton constructed by Ivey–Dancer–Wang.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The classification is for non-Ricci-flat, κ-noncollapsed, cohomogeneity-one steady gradient Ricci solitons in dimensions four and five.
sections.unique_caveat: The result does not purport to classify higher dimensions, other cohomogeneities, or Ricci-flat cases.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract combines a named conjecture resolution with a dimension-specific classification into explicit known solitons.

sections.title: Global well-posedness for the energy-critical focusing NLS on T³
sections.abstract: The authors prove global well-posedness for the focusing quintic nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the standard three-dimensional torus for initial data below the mass-corrected energy and Sobolev thresholds determined by the Euclidean ground state.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove global well-posedness below both stated mass-corrected energy and Sobolev-norm thresholds, using an invariant region, a nonnegative energy decomposition, and a contradiction argument for finite-time bounds.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The equation is the focusing quintic NLS on the standard three-dimensional torus, with initial data strictly below the stated Euclidean-ground-state thresholds.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract covers the subthreshold regime only; it makes no claim at or above the threshold.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper claims a global result for an energy-critical focusing equation on a compact domain under explicit ground-state thresholds, connecting periodic profile analysis with a recent Euclidean scattering theorem.

sections.title: Butler's conjecture for K3 curves
sections.abstract: The authors prove two cases of Butler's conjectures for curves of genus at least eight by establishing the result on curves lying on Picard-rank-one K3 surfaces and using deformation and openness.
sections.claimed_result: For g≥8, the authors prove Butler's conjectures in the rank-one case and in the range μ(E)>2g−2, under the stated general-curve and semistability framework.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The proof reduces by deformation and openness to a Brill–Noether–Petri general curve on a K3 surface of Picard rank one; the covered cases are rank one and μ(E)>2g−2.
sections.unique_caveat: The result covers only the two stated cases for genus at least eight, not the full conjecture for all ranks and slopes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract addresses a named conjectural family and combines wall-crossing for coherent systems with a K3-surface construction; the theorem covers two rank/slope regimes.
